hypotheses.statement: Some responses are recorded more than once

evidence.text: 15 groups of response rows share the same (customer_id, campaign_id, response_date, revenue) with count > 1, covering 30 rows; per the wiki deduplication rule these are duplicates of a single response.
The known duplicate-load incident (ETL restart loading the same responses file twice) is the documented cause of such duplicates.

hypotheses.statement: Some customers are in both treatment and control of the same campaign

evidence.text: Campaign 103 has 25 customers with more than one distinct grp in contacts, violating the disjoint treatment/control policy.
The data dictionary states a customer must be in exactly one group per campaign.

hypotheses.statement: Some responses are dated before the customer was contacted

evidence.text: 12 responses join to a contact row of the same customer and campaign with response_date < contact_date; the attribution rule says such responses are never attributed.

hypotheses.statement: Some campaigns end before they start

evidence.text: count(*) of campaigns with end_date < start_date is 0.

hypotheses.statement: Treatment beats control on response rate in every campaign

evidence.text: Rates are computed on distinct customers (deduplicated contacts and responses), so duplicate response rows do not inflate them.

hypotheses.statement: Some responses in campaign 101 are recorded more than once

evidence.text: count(*) of duplicate (customer, campaign, date, revenue) groups restricted to campaign_id = 101 is 0.
The 15 duplicate groups found overall are not in campaign 101 (campaign 102 alone has 15 duplicate groups).

hypotheses.statement: Some responses arrived more than 30 days after their campaign ended

evidence.text: 6 responses have response_date > campaign end_date + 30 days, all dated 2026-11-10.
All 6 belong to campaign 101 'Autumn data bundle' (end_date 2026-10-01), i.e. 40 days after the campaign ended.

hypotheses.statement: Win-back October reduced churn among contacted customers

evidence.text: Campaign 104 'Win-back October' exists (sms, 2026-10-01..2026-10-15), but the warehouse has only campaigns, contacts and responses tables.

No column matching churn/retention/status exists in any table, so churn cannot be measured; the churn definition (no paid activity for 30 consecutive days) requires paid-activity data that is not present.

hypotheses.statement: Some customers were contacted twice within the same group of one campaign

evidence.text: Grouping contacts by (customer_id, campaign_id, grp) and keeping groups with count(*) > 1 returns no rows, so no customer has more than one contact row within a single group of a campaign.
